outcomes.title: Relational Concepts
outcomes.description: Understand relational database concepts (tables, keys, relationships) and explain why normalization matters.
outcomes.competencyThreshold: Can explain the purpose of primary keys, foreign keys, and 3NF to a non-technical stakeholder.

outcomes.title: Read SQL
outcomes.description: Read and interpret SQL queries to identify what data they retrieve.
outcomes.competencyThreshold: Given an unfamiliar SQL query with JOINs and aggregation, can describe in plain English what data it returns.

outcomes.title: Data Quality Awareness
outcomes.description: Recognize when data needs cleaning and describe common data quality issues.
outcomes.competencyThreshold: Can identify 3+ data quality issues in a messy dataset and explain why each matters for downstream analysis.

outcomes.title: Write SQL
outcomes.description: Write SQL queries to extract, transform, and aggregate data from relational databases.
outcomes.competencyThreshold: Can independently write a multi-table JOIN with aggregation and filtering to answer a business question.

outcomes.title: Design Normalized Schema
outcomes.description: Design a normalized database schema (3NF) for a given business problem.
outcomes.competencyThreshold: Given business requirements, can produce an ERD and CREATE TABLE statements in 3NF with correct keys and constraints.

outcomes.title: Build ETL Pipeline
outcomes.description: Use Python (pandas, sqlalchemy) to build a complete ETL pipeline.
outcomes.competencyThreshold: Can build an end-to-end pipeline that extracts from 2+ sources, transforms with pandas, and loads into a database via sqlalchemy.

outcomes.title: Cloud Database Access
outcomes.description: Connect to cloud databases and run queries in browser-based SQL environments.
outcomes.competencyThreshold: Can configure an AWS RDS instance, connect from Python, and execute queries remotely.

outcomes.title: Design Trade-offs
outcomes.description: Evaluate design trade-offs (normalization vs. denormalization) for specific use cases.
outcomes.competencyThreshold: Can justify denormalization decisions with performance data and articulate the trade-offs during oral defense.

outcomes.title: Query Optimization
outcomes.description: Optimize queries for performance and design effective indexes.
outcomes.competencyThreshold: Can analyze an EXPLAIN plan, identify bottlenecks, and design indexes that improve query performance by 30%+.

misconceptions.description: SELECT * is fine for production queries
misconceptions.remediation: Studio exercise: compare execution plans of SELECT * vs specific columns on a 1M row table. Measure performance difference.

misconceptions.description: More JOINs always means slower queries
misconceptions.remediation: Pair exercise: compare query plans for subquery vs JOIN approaches to the same question. Show when JOINs are actually faster.

misconceptions.description: Third Normal Form is always the right design choice
misconceptions.remediation: Case study: data warehouse star schema vs 3NF OLTP. Show where denormalization improves read performance at the cost of write complexity.

misconceptions.description: Python is too slow for real data work — just use SQL
misconceptions.remediation: Demo: tasks easy in pandas but painful in SQL (reshaping, regex cleaning, API calls). Show pandas+SQL is more powerful than either alone.

misconceptions.description: ETL pipelines should load all data at once to be efficient
misconceptions.remediation: Build pipeline that crashes at row 50K of 100K. Show chunked loading with error handling recovers gracefully.

misconceptions.description: NoSQL databases are newer and better than SQL databases
misconceptions.remediation: CAP theorem exercise: for 3 business scenarios, determine whether SQL or NoSQL is the better fit and explain why.

misconceptions.description: Cloud databases are automatically faster than local ones
misconceptions.remediation: Benchmark: same query on local PostgreSQL vs micro AWS RDS instance. Discuss network latency, instance sizing, and when cloud makes sense.

misconceptions.description: If the data loads without errors, it must be clean
misconceptions.remediation: Give students a CSV that loads perfectly but contains duplicates, type mismatches, and impossible values. Ask them to find 5 issues.

guardrails.title: No PII in Public Repos
guardrails.description: Student projects use synthetic or public datasets only. No personally identifiable information in GitHub repos or Canvas submissions.
guardrails.enforcement: Project rubric includes 'Data Privacy' dimension. Automated scan of repo for common PII patterns before grading.

guardrails.title: AI Attribution Required
guardrails.description: All AI tool usage must be documented in an AI Attribution Log: date, tool, prompt summary, output summary, modifications made.
guardrails.enforcement: AI Attribution Log is a required deliverable in Projects 1-3. Missing log = incomplete submission.

guardrails.title: Oral Defense Verifies Understanding
guardrails.description: Project 3 team oral defense ensures students can explain and defend their technical choices without AI assistance.
guardrails.enforcement: 20% of Project 3 grade is oral defense. AIAS Level 0 during defense. Individual follow-up questions to each team member.

guardrails.title: Uniform Rubrics Across Pathways
guardrails.description: All students assessed against identical rubric dimensions regardless of their adaptive pathway through the material.
guardrails.enforcement: 5-dimension rubric per project. Same thresholds for Excellent/Proficient/Developing for all students.

guardrails.title: No AI on Formative Quizzes
guardrails.description: Weekly quizzes test foundational knowledge without AI assistance (AIAS Level 0).
guardrails.enforcement: Canvas quiz settings: timed, no browser navigation, randomized question order.

guardrails.title: L-C-E Progression Documented
guardrails.description: Each outcome maps to L-C-E level. Evidence collected at each level supports AACSB Assurance of Learning.
guardrails.enforcement: Course spec maps outcomes → evidence → assessment. Aggregated results reported per AACSB cycle.

guardrails.title: AIAS Levels Per Assignment
guardrails.description: Each assessment has a declared AI Assessment Integration Scale level. Level 0 = no AI, Level 2 = AI-assisted with attribution, Level 3 = AI as collaborative tool.
guardrails.enforcement: AIAS level printed on every assignment. Projects 1-2 = Level 2, Project 3 = Level 3, Quizzes = Level 0, Oral Defense = Level 0.

guardrails.title: Process Documentation Required
guardrails.description: Projects require documentation of methodology: approaches tried, AI tools used, lessons from failures, how AI output was validated.
guardrails.enforcement: Process Documentation section in every project rubric (10-15% weight). Missing = maximum 'Developing' on that dimension.
